events.title: First Lancaster House conference
events.summary: Kenya's constitutional future is negotiated in London under Colonial Secretary Iain Macleod. There is no agreement, and Macleod issues an interim constitution.

events.title: KADU is formed
events.summary: Leading politicians who refuse to join Kenyatta's KANU form the Kenya African Democratic Union, led by Ronald Ngala. It brings together smaller parties, including Moi's Kalenjin Political Alliance and Masinde Muliro's Baluhya Political Union.

events.title: KANU is formed
events.summary: James Gichuru re-establishes the banned Kenya African Union, and on 14 May it becomes the Kenya African National Union after merging with Tom Mboya's Kenya Independence Movement. KANU will rule Kenya for nearly 40 years.

events.title: The Kennedy Airlift gets its name
events.summary: Senator John F. Kennedy arranges a $100,000 donation to fly the autumn 1960 group of East African students to colleges in North America. The programme, started by Tom Mboya, brought hundreds of students between 1959 and 1963.

events.title: Legio Maria church founded
events.summary: Legio Maria, an African initiated church among the Luo of western Kenya, breaks away from the Catholic lay movement it grew out of. Its followers believe Simeo Ondetto to be the returned Son of God.

events.title: Maasai Mara game reserve
events.summary: The Maasai Mara national game reserve in Narok County is established. It borders Tanzania's Serengeti and hosts the great wildebeest migration.

events.title: Strathmore founded in Nairobi
events.summary: Strathmore, now a chartered university in Nairobi, is founded.

events.title: KANU wins the 1961 election
events.summary: General elections are held in February 1961. KANU wins 19 of the 53 elected seats.

events.title: A foreign ministry for independent Kenya
events.summary: Kenya's Ministry of Foreign Affairs is established after independence to run the country's foreign relations.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Ministry of Foreign and Diaspora Affairs (Kenya)

events.title: An anthem from a Pokomo lullaby
events.summary: A five-member commission writes "Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu" in Kiswahili for independence, setting it to a tune Pokomo mothers sang to their children. It is one of the first anthems to be specially commissioned.

events.title: Chemchemi Cultural Center opens
events.summary: An arts and cultural centre, Chemchemi, opens in Nairobi.

events.title: Goethe-Institut opens in Kenya
events.summary: The German cultural institute opens its Kenyan branch.

events.title: Last Lancaster House conference
events.summary: The third conference in London finalises the constitutional arrangements for Kenya's independence as a Dominion. The first two met in 1960 and 1962.

events.title: Malcolm MacDonald becomes Governor
events.summary: London replaces Governor Patrick Renison with Malcolm MacDonald to oversee the transition. A timetable follows: elections in May, self-government in June.

events.title: Plantation workers' union formed
events.summary: Several unions merge into the Kenya Plantation and Agricultural Workers Union, representing tea, coffee and other farm workers. Its head office is in Nakuru.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Kenya Plantation and Agricultural Workers Union

events.title: Relations with West Germany
events.summary: Kenya and the Federal Republic of Germany establish diplomatic relations in the year of independence.

events.title: The coat of arms
events.summary: Kenya's coat of arms shows two lions holding spears and a shield in the national colours, with KANU's rooster on the shield. The scroll beneath reads Harambee, "pulling together".
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Coat of arms of Kenya

events.title: North Eastern Region created
events.summary: Britain announces a new North Eastern Region carved out of the Northern Frontier District, covering Wajir, Mandera and Garissa. The Northern Province is split across three regions.

events.title: Somalia breaks off relations with Britain
events.summary: Unsatisfied with the new region, the Somali Republic severs diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom. The dispute over the north will outlast colonial rule.

events.title: KADU loses on a majimbo platform
events.summary: Ronald Ngala's KADU had campaigned for majimbo, a regional system of government. It loses to KANU and joins with smaller parties in opposition.

events.title: Northern seats left empty
events.summary: Five House seats and three Senate seats go unfilled because of the secessionist conflict on the border with Somalia. The north enters independence without its elected members.

events.title: KANU wins the general election
events.summary: Voters elect a House of Representatives and a Senate in the last election before independence. KANU wins 83 of 124 House seats and 18 of 38 Senate seats.

events.title: Madaraka: self-rule begins
events.summary: Kenya attains internal self-government and Jomo Kenyatta is sworn in as Prime Minister. The day is still marked every year as Madaraka Day.

events.title: Three leaders promise a federation
events.summary: Kenyatta, Julius Nyerere and Milton Obote meet in Nairobi and declare that an East African Federation will be formed by the end of the year. By 1964 it has not come to pass.

events.title: Tom Mboya takes Justice
events.summary: Kenyatta appoints Tom Mboya Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs. He holds the post until December 1964.

events.title: University of East Africa founded
events.summary: A single university is established to serve Kenya, Tanganyika and Uganda, with a college in each. Nairobi's college is one of the three.

events.title: Kenyatta meets settler farmers at Nakuru
events.summary: Kenyatta meets 300 white farmers at Nakuru as part of an effort to keep good relations with settlers. Settlers had been leaving at about 700 a month.

events.title: The coastal strip's future is settled
events.summary: Under an agreement dated 8 October, the Sultan of Zanzibar agrees that his sovereignty over the coastal Protectorate of Kenya ends at independence. The strip had been nominally leased from Zanzibar since 1895.

events.title: A law against disrespecting the Prime Minister
events.summary: Kenyatta's government makes it a criminal offence to show disrespect to the Prime Minister. The punishment is exile.

events.title: Fighting grows in the north
events.summary: Security in the Northern Frontier District declines fast as shifta fighters begin attacking police and army posts directly. Historians date the Shifta War from this year.

events.title: Britain will not redraw the border
events.summary: The British government declares there will be no altering of Kenya's frontier without the decision of the new Kenyan government. Somalia's claim to the north is left to Nairobi.

events.title: Independence
events.summary: Kenya becomes independent as a Commonwealth realm, with Elizabeth II as Queen of Kenya and Malcolm MacDonald as Governor-General. Kenyatta remains Prime Minister.

events.title: Midnight at Uhuru Gardens
events.summary: Independence is declared at midnight at the site in Nairobi now kept as Uhuru Gardens. A mũgumo tree is said to mark the spot where the colonial flag came down and Kenya's went up.

events.title: The flag is adopted
events.summary: The national flag, based mainly on the flag of KANU, is officially adopted on independence day. Its black, red and green go back to the Kenya African Union's flag of the early 1950s.

events.title: The UN Security Council backs Kenya's membership
events.summary: The Security Council unanimously adopts Resolution 185, recommending that the General Assembly admit Kenya to the United Nations.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: United Nations Security Council Resolution 185

events.title: Emergency in the North Eastern Region
events.summary: Two weeks after independence, the government declares a state of emergency in the North Eastern Region. The conflict runs until 1967.

events.title: National Youth Service founded
events.summary: The National Youth Service is established to train young people in national matters.

events.title: The Kenya Army is formed
events.summary: Kenya's land army is formed as British units are handed over around independence.

events.title: The Kenya Navy is formed
events.summary: Kenya's navy is formed. It is headquartered in Mombasa.

events.title: The Kenya Air Force is formed
events.summary: Kenya's air force is established as a branch of the armed forces.

events.title: Kenya becomes a republic
events.summary: On the first anniversary of independence Kenya becomes a republic and Jomo Kenyatta becomes its first President. He holds office until his death in 1978.

events.title: COTU is founded
events.summary: The Central Organization of Trade Unions is founded as the Kenya Federation of Labour and the African Workers' Congress are dissolved. It becomes Kenya's national trade union centre.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Central Organization of Trade Unions

events.title: Kenya National Library Service set up
events.summary: An Act of Parliament establishes the Kenya National Library Service to run the national library and public libraries.

events.title: Kenya Red Cross established
events.summary: Kenya's national Red Cross society is established.

events.title: Ahero irrigation scheme
events.summary: The Ahero irrigation scheme is set up.

events.title: Jomo Kenyatta Foundation founded
events.summary: The Jomo Kenyatta Foundation, an educational publisher owned by the state, is founded.

events.title: Meru National Park
events.summary: Meru National Park, east of Meru, is created. Joy and George Adamson raised Elsa the lioness of Born Free there.

events.title: The Central Bank of Kenya is founded
events.summary: The Central Bank of Kenya is founded after the East African Currency Board is dissolved. It becomes the country's monetary authority.

events.title: The Kenya People's Union is formed
events.summary: Jaramogi Oginga Odinga leads a breakaway from KANU to form the socialist Kenya People's Union. It will be banned in 1969.

events.title: Kenya creates its national honours
events.summary: The Order of the Burning Spear, the Order of the Golden Heart and the Distinguished Service Medal are established on the same day. They are awarded by the President for service to the nation.
events.source_name: Wikipedia: Orders, decorations, and medals of Kenya

events.title: The "little general election"
events.summary: After 29 MPs leave KANU for the Kenya People's Union, a constitutional amendment forces them to seek re-election. The KPU wins the most votes, but KANU wins more seats.

events.title: Lake Nakuru National Park
events.summary: Lake Nakuru National Park is established.

events.title: Ol Donyo Sabuk National Park
events.summary: A national park is created on Ol Donyo Sabuk mountain in Machakos.

events.title: Malindi Marine National Park
events.summary: A marine national park is created in the Indian Ocean at Malindi. It is said to be the oldest marine park in Africa.

events.title: Shimba Hills National Reserve
events.summary: The Shimba Hills reserve near Mombasa is created to protect coastal rainforest, woodland and grassland. Over half of Kenya's rare plants grow there.

events.title: Watamu Marine National Park
events.summary: Watamu Marine National Park is established, one of Kenya's first marine parks. Its coral gardens lie 300 metres from the shore.

events.title: Mount Elgon National Park
events.summary: The Kenyan side of Mount Elgon is gazetted as a national park. Uganda's side follows in 1992.

events.title: USIU-Africa founded
events.summary: United States International University-Africa, a private university in Nairobi, is founded.

events.title: The Kisumu massacre
events.summary: The presidential guard and police shoot civilians in Kisumu. The government puts the toll at 11 dead; other sources say close to 100.

events.title: A one-party election
events.summary: In the first general election since independence, KANU is the only party, after the Kenya People's Union was banned on 30 October. Kenyatta is the sole presidential candidate and is returned without a vote.
